message.content: {"criteria":[{"id":"C1","level":"Adequate","mark":6,"evidence":[{"where":"Introduction","quote":"Thus, only one satellite is required. This also just allows for simplicity in communications, reduces cost"},{"where":"Introduction","quote":"The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM) for research and/or education."}],"reasoning":"Mission, rationale, single-satellite choice and users are addressed, but user/operator identification is vague and not clearly separated. Rationale is well argued but some references are weak (Wikipedia-sourced claims, unsupported 30% acidity statement). Operator not explicitly named."},{"id":"C2","level":"Adequate","mark":5,"evidence":[{"where":"Orbit","quote":"Specifically, an altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of $ 97.7924^{\\circ} $ for the satellite to remain sun-synchronous."},{"where":"Launch","quote":"The proposed satellite will thus use the Vega E rocket as a launch vehicle"},{"where":"Mission Duration & EOL","quote":"However, the ZYZZsat is without thrust capability and so must use a ‘passive’ strategy."}],"reasoning":"Orbit, COE table, STK access and ground track are provided, but the COE table has errors (semi-major axis, RAAN explanation, argument of latitude misdefined as zero). Launch vehicle Vega E is not yet built and launch-site latitude/equator logic is inconsistent. EOL section is incomplete (drag sail sentence truncated) and contradicts the no-thrust claim. Maneuvers stated as only EOL but no delta-v given. Ground control facility is selected but only one station, and the stated 'Tasmanian facility' contradicts later Australia-focused claims."},{"id":"C3","level":"Adequate","mark":4,"evidence":[{"where":"Conclusion","quote":"A polar sun-synchronous orbit allows for consistent illumination of the oceans while maintaining a constant sun angle."}],"reasoning":"Conclusion summarises the design and notes launch uncertainty, but largely restates content without quantified outcomes or critical evaluation of trade-offs and EOL risks."},{"id":"C4","level":"Adequate","mark":5,"evidence":[{"where":"Contents","quote":"Executive Summary ..... 2"},{"where":"Bibliography","quote":"[6] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_in_spaceflight. [Online]."}],"reasoning":"Clear headings and figure labels, but mixed formatting, table with duplicated/mislabelled access numbers (13 repeated), typos and grammar errors, truncated sentences, and a Wikipedia source breaching the brief. Reference style is inconsistent and cites web links without dates."}],"requirements":[{"id":"R1","met":"yes","where":"Introduction"},{"id":"R2","met":"yes","where":"Introduction"},{"id":"R3","met":"partial","where":"Introduction"},{"id":"R4","met":"partial","where":"Launch"},{"id":"R5","met":"partial","where":"Orbit"},{"id":"R6","met":"partial","where":"Orbit"},{"id":"R7","met":"yes","where":"Ground Control & Communications"},{"id":"R8","met":"partial","where":"Mission Duration & EOL"},{"id":"R9","met":"yes","where":"Ground Control & Communications"},{"id":"R10","met":"partial","where":"Orbit"},{"id":"R11","met":"no","where":"Bibliography"}],"technical_issues":[{"where":"Orbit","issue":"Argument of latitude is stated as 0° while also described as undefined; RAAN of 27.33° is attributed to launch site without justification; sun-synchronous RAAN rate described as 360° per year is correct but phrasing of 1°/day should be stated as 0.9856°/day."},{"where":"Launch","issue":"Kourou latitude (~5.2°N) is cited to justify maximising launch efficiency, but a 97.8° inclination orbit is retrograde; the claim that the launch window count depends on latitude versus inclination is muddled."},{"where":"Mission Duration & EOL","issue":"Claims uncontrolled descent needs least energy yet notes no thrust; drag sail discussion is truncated and no quantitative decay/ballistic analysis given for 600 km altitude."},{"where":"Ground Control & Communications","issue":"Claims near-polar ground station maximises passes, but contact durations and pass counts are inconsistent with the 15-access table (access 13 duplicated)."}],"overall":"A coherent sun-synchronous Earth-observation concept with STK evidence, but the report has incomplete EOL text, a numerical COE table with errors, a Wikipedia source, unclear launch and operator details, and presentation flaws. Solid but adequate overall."}
